agent_teams.label: Agent collaboration
agent_teams.description: One capability for multi-agent work: the main model chooses whether to answer directly, delegate to a sub-agent, or run independent workstreams in parallel. No fixed role presets, no separate Swarm switch.
agent_teams.tradeoffs: Delegated and parallel turns can spend more tokens than a single agent. The main model decides when the extra work is worth it; turning this off disables all sub-agent dispatch for new turns.

wakeups.label: Wakeups
wakeups.description: Lets the agent pick a thread back up by itself to carry on a task: at a time, or every few minutes. Pending wakeups show in the chat tray and the Status panel, where you can cancel any of them.
wakeups.tradeoffs: A wakeup that fires while the thread is idle starts a turn by itself, which costs as much as any turn; checking every 5 minutes can take up to 24 turns over two hours. Turning this off cancels every pending wakeup.

site_crawl.label: Site crawling (experimental)
site_crawl.description: Gives the agent WebMap and WebCrawl tools: list a site's URLs, then crawl whole sections into workspace files for multi-page research (docs sites, document archives).
site_crawl.tradeoffs: Crawling bills per delivered page up to the call's page limit, so a broad crawl costs more than targeted fetches. Experimental — behavior and pricing may change.

scratchpad.label: Scratchpad and working notes
scratchpad.description: Gives the agent a scratchpad folder in each thread for its intermediate files, and has it keep running notes there: key findings, decisions and why, and corrections you give mid-task. The notes carry a long task through after older messages in the thread are summarized.
scratchpad.tradeoffs: The agent spends a few extra tool calls per task keeping its notes. The scratchpad and its notes are deleted when you archive the thread, so keep anything you want to last in the workspace's own files.

native_runtime.label: Native agent runtime (experimental)
native_runtime.description: Runs a thread inside a vendor agent CLI instead of the PTC agent. The CLI owns its prompt, tool loop, session and cache; Conductor carries the thread, history, cancellation and workspace transport. Codex is end-to-end today; the other CLIs are still being verified.
native_runtime.tradeoffs: A native thread cannot use Conductor's PTC tool loop, subagents, memory injection or HITL approvals yet. Answer quality and cost follow the selected CLI account and policy, not Conductor's model settings. Keep this off unless you are testing the path.

agentTeams.title: Agent collaboration
agentTeams.line: Single agent, sub-agent teams and parallel Swarm are selected by the main model; no fixed role presets.
agentTeams.description: No fixed-role presets. The main model chooses a direct answer, a sub-agent team, or parallel execution; users see one capability.
agentTeams.modeDirect: Direct: the task is simple enough to answer without splitting.
agentTeams.modeDelegate: Sub-agent team: the main model delegates research, data and report work as needed.
agentTeams.modeParallel: Parallel Swarm: independent workstreams run together and are synthesized at the end.
agentTeams.boundary: Users do not pick roles or configure a per-thread team. Agent progress, stop and results remain visible; spend and concurrency stay runtime-controlled.

models.explainerBackgroundBody: Never runs a conversation, only the work around one, so a faster, cheaper model is usually enough.
